query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 5 at.% Ni to the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs) can improve its ductility and toughness by 20% and 30%, respectively, due to the formation of a face-centered cubic (FCC) phase that enhances grain boundary sliding and reduces the Peierls stress.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs) in the as-cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of 5 at.% Ni to the HfZrTi HEAs
generation.conditions: Vacuum arc melting and subsequent annealing at 1000°C for 2 hours
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary sliding and reduction of Peierls stress
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in ductility and 30% increase in toughness
generation.baseline: As-cast HfZrTi HEAs without Ni addition
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in ductility and toughness may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and microstructure of the alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural characterization of the HfZrTi HEAs with and without Ni addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of 5 at.% Ni does not result in a significant improvement in ductility and toughness (less than 10% increase), the hypothesis is falsified.
